headline: NVIDIA Surges 31.71% as Jensen Huang's Return Sets Off a Market-Wide AI Rally
body_html:
NVIDIA shares were up 31.71% at midday Monday, by far the largest move of the session, after Jensen Huang's return to the company's top job. President Trump said he had persuaded the board to bring Huang back, and investors treated the news as relief following a brutal selloff in the stock. Prices are not final.

The rally spread well beyond one name. Semiconductors averaged a gain of 12.80%, with Micron up 18.54%, Arm up 16.15% and TSMC up 15.30%. Of the 663 stocks tracked, 611 were higher and 50 were lower. Financials added 8.72%, the next-best sector, while Materials and Industrials each gained more than 4%.

Into the close, the question is whether NVIDIA can hold its gains after such a sharp jump. Traders are also watching headlines about rising Fed rate-hike odds, and TSMC's pause in advanced chip shipments to China. CrowdStrike, down 10.35%, is the day's weakest large name. The next session is Tuesday, November 24.

briefs.headline: TSMC Rebounds 15.30% After a Rough Week
briefs.body: The chip foundry bounced sharply after sliding about 20% over the past week. That slide was blamed on worries around NVIDIA and fresh US chip curbs on China. The company has paused advanced chip shipments to China, so that remains a risk heading into the close.

briefs.headline: Micron Climbs 18.54% as Memory Selloff Reverses
briefs.body: Micron jumped as chip stocks recovered, lifted by NVIDIA's leadership news. Citi has said the recent memory selloff looked overdone and that AI memory demand is holding up. A separate report noted the shares had fallen to a low multiple of annualized earnings before the bounce.

briefs.headline: Connectivity Chipmakers Fill the Top-Gainer List
briefs.body: MaxLinear rose 22.77%, Credo Technology 21.12% and Astera Labs 21.02%, all trading just behind NVIDIA among the day's best performers. Bloom Energy added 18.65% and was named in reports on the AI-linked rebound. Together they show how widely the rally has spread across the AI supply chain.

briefs.headline: Financials Take Second Place Among Sectors
briefs.body: Financials averaged a gain of 8.72%, well behind Semiconductors at 12.80% but ahead of every other group. Materials rose 4.52% and Industrials 4.44%. Materials also drew attention from a report that Congo has again halted cobalt exports to curb oversupply and support prices. Energy trailed at 1.79%.

briefs.headline: CrowdStrike Slides 10.35% Against the Tide
briefs.body: CrowdStrike was the largest decliner as the market rose. Burlington Stores fell 4.52% and Iovance Biotherapeutics 4.42%. Only 50 of the 663 stocks tracked were lower, so the weakness was narrow. The data gives no cause for the cybersecurity name's drop.

briefs.headline: Mega-Caps Join In, and Rate Worries Linger
briefs.body: Tesla gained 12.19% and Apple 2.05%, while reports had Meta up about 6% and Palantir higher on the AI rebound. One headline pointed to a jump in Fed rate-hike odds, and another said Wall Street's fear gauge flashed a buy signal. Those are the cross-currents to watch into the close.
